subject: Dedicated pool: tiered pricing + GPU mix recommendation
messages:
From: Elena Soto <procurement@nimbus.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: CFO Nimbus <cfo@nimbus.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: Dedicated GPU pool options for large-scale inference

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking a look — quick background: Nimbus is planning to move a user-facing generative-search product to a dedicated inference pool. Our rough target is 6-8B tokens/day on average with burst capacity to 15B/day during marketing pushes. Latency SLO is 95th p50 ~ <120ms for standard chat flows.

We currently prefer H100-class performance for latency-sensitive models but are cost-sensitive and open to mixed fleets. Specifically we need:
- A baseline committed pool with a throughput guarantee (tokens/hour or GPU-hour SLA)
- Pricing for 6/12/24-month commits with any volume discounts or ramp credits
- Guidance on memory tradeoffs: whether A100 (40/80GB) vs H100 (80GB) vs L40S (48GB) makes sense given our mix (long-context reranking + embeddings-heavy prefiltering + conversational generation)

Attached is a simple demand estimate (nimbus-demand-sheet.xlsx). Can you share a tiered pricing proposal and an initial recommendation for GPU mix?

Best,
Elena
Procurement, Nimbus Analytics
[attachment: nimbus-demand-sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimbus.ai>, Procurement (Nimbus Analytics) <procurement@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Dedicated GPU pool options for large-scale inference

Elena — thanks for the demand sheet and context. I've reviewed the numbers with our solutions team and put together an initial tiered proposal (attached) and a short tradeoffs summary below. Happy to hop on a call to walk through the modeling.

Executive summary / recommended starting point:
- Baseline pool: Mixed H100+L40S with H100 reserved for latency-critical routing (peak generation) and L40S for embeddings and high-throughput prefilter.
- Suggested starting capacity: 6x H100 (80GB) + 10x L40S (48GB) as a baseline reserve; autoscale burst to additional H100s during marketing spikes. This configuration targets ~6-8B tokens/day sustained and headroom to 15B when combined with bursting.
- Pricing model: flat committed GPU-hour + additive network & support. We provide a throughput SLA for committed capacity (99.5% uptime on reserved GPUs and prioritized scheduling for reserved requests).

High-level perf/$ and memory tradeoffs:
- H100 (80GB): best single-instance latency for large-context generation and heavy attention; highest perf/token but also highest price per GPU-hour. Ideal for the small set of endpoints that must hit tight 95th percentile latency.
- A100 (40/80GB): good all-around performer for older transformer stacks and workloads that are more memory-bound; lower perf than H100 for same clock/gflops but cheaper per-hour. Consider A100 where model codepaths are stable and you can tolerate slightly higher latency.
- L40S (48GB): excellent perf/$ for high-throughput embedding and reranking workloads; smaller memory than H100 but cheaper and denser — good for batched workloads and prefiltering.

Draft tiered discounts (attached PDF has line-item math):
- 6-month commit: 12% discount on list GPU-hour rates + 10% ramp credit applied over first 2 months
- 12-month commit: 20% discount + 2 months ramp credit (reduced billing for months 1-2)
- 24-month commit: 30% discount + 3 months ramp credit + optional accelerated-invoice model (prepay at 3% additional discount)

Perf/$ examples (illustrative):
- H100 baseline: $3.10 / GPU-hour (list) -> $2.48 with 20% discount (12-mo) ; ~0.85M tokens per GPU-hour on your 8k context gen model -> ~ $0.0029 per 1k tokens for generation path (illustrative)
- L40S baseline: $1.10 / GPU-hour -> $0.88 with 20% discount ; ~1.8M tokens per GPU-hour for batched embedding job -> ~ $0.0005 per 1k tokens for embedding path

Attachments: redwood-tiered-proposal-v1.pdf (pricing grid + SLA language), throughput-modeling.csv (detailed perf assumptions).

Next steps: if the mix above looks reasonable, we'll produce a countersigned quote and propose a pilot: 3-month evaluation (prorated) to validate perf assumptions and instrument our tracing hooks into your staging traffic.

-Vivek
Director, Dedicated Sales
Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-tiered-proposal-v1.pdf (proposal)]
[attachment: throughput-modeling.csv (csv)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Dedicated GPU pool options for large-scale inference

Vivek — quick internal note before we finalize:
- The discount schedule looks reasonable but I think we should tighten the 6/12/24 bands for this account given their projected growth and strategic value. Proposal: 15% (6-mo), 25% (12-mo), 33% (24-mo) with 2 months free on the 24-mo. We can reserve that in HubSpot as an internal playbook.
- SLA language: 99.5% is okay, but they asked specifically for prioritized scheduling and tokens/hour guarantees; let's add a quant clause: 'Guaranteed minimum reserved throughput expressed as X tokens/hour per reserved H100 equivalency' and an uptime credit schedule in days. Legal can draft the exact wording but we should include it on the quote.
- GPU mix: offer two packaged SKUs in the quote: "Latency-Optimized" (8x H100 + 6x L40S) and "Cost-Optimized" (4x H100 + 16x L40S + optional A100 pool). Explain a migration path (start cost-optimized, route 10-20% traffic to latency-optimized).

Ben — can you run a quick margin check on the tighter discounts and confirm whether 2 months free on 24-mo keeps GP margin above 48%? If yes, I'll bake that into the customer-facing deck and we can send a follow-up today.

-Marissa
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@nimbus.ai>, Procurement (Nimbus Analytics) <procurement@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Dedicated GPU pool options for large-scale inference — Proposal and next steps

Elena — following internal review we've tightened the offer and attached an updated quote. Key changes from the initial draft:

1) Tiered pricing (finalized):
- 6-month commit: 15% discount on list GPU-hour rates + 10% ramp credit (applies first 2 months)
- 12-month commit: 25% discount + 2 months ramp credit
- 24-month commit: 33% discount + 2 months free + option to prepay for an extra 3% off

2) SKU choices (pick one as starting config):
- Latency-Optimized SKU: 8x H100 (80GB) + 6x L40S (48GB) — reserved for latency-critical endpoints, ~8B tokens/day sustained
- Cost-Optimized SKU: 4x H100 + 16x L40S + optional A100 overflow pool — optimized for embeddings/rerank and batched inference, ~6B tokens/day sustained at lower unit cost

3) SLA and guarantees:
- Committed reserved throughput defined as a minimum token-hour capacity per reserved H100 equivalency. 99.5% reserved GPU availability target; service credits for missed availability to be defined in SOW. We will provide prioritized scheduling for reserved requests and tracing hooks for per-route cost/latency analysis.

4) Pilot option:
- 6-week pilot (prorated) with the chosen SKU to validate perf assumptions and routing rules. Pilot consumption applies to commit if you transition to a 12/24 month within 60 days of pilot end.

Attachments: updated quote PDF + SOW draft (DocuSign link below).

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/4321

Thanks — talk soon.
-Vivek
